sources.entry: mtdvio/every-programmer-should-know: a collection of (mostly) technical things every software developer should know about

summary.one_liner: A curated, opinionated link list of technical books, articles, talks, and practice sites that the author recommends to programmers of any skill level.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome"-style list of resources rather than software. It is organized into topic sections such as Algorithms, Data Structures, Numbers, Strings, Latency, Time, Memory, Distributed Systems, Security, Architecture, Code Design, Practices, Career, Remote Work, Soft Skills, and Platform Engineering. Each entry is a link to a book, article, video, or site, often with a short note. The README says the picks are highly opinionated, not backed by science, and listed in no particular order. It also includes sections for coding practice sites, papers on programming, free programming books, and open source licenses. The README also contains a promotional quiz banner at the top, which this summary ignores.
use_cases: Learning security basics for web developers
Reading about distributed systems and architecture
Researching developer career and salary resources
notable: Covers a broad range of programming topics, from floating point and Unicode to platform engineering and career advice
Sections for coding practice sites such as LeetCode, Codewars, and Exercism
Includes classic papers and books such as SICP, Code Complete, and Designing Data-Intensive Applications
Organized by topic with a mix of books, videos, and articles marked by icons
caveats: Explicitly opinionated and not backed by science, per the README
Items are links only; the repo does not host the content itself
Some resources may be dated or no longer available; the README does not address maintenance
